consensus_summary: Primary consensus: spiritual freedom from bondage to sin, death, and the law's condemnation through Christ/Spirit, for holiness, love, and service rather than license. Common alternatives: Jubilee as typological release, liberty of conscience in adiaphora, socio-political liberation; rarer free will or pure autonomy (condemned).
book_summary: Liberty is the King's jubilee release out of the slaver's house (sin, Egypt, Babylon) into God's household, inheritance, and service: a change of masters, never the absence of one. Its constitution is the perfect law of liberty; license is the counterfeit that returns to bondage.
consensus_core_identification: spiritual freedom/emancipation from sin's bondage through Christ into righteous service (not license)
book_core_identification: King's jubilee release from bondage (sin/Egypt/Babylon) into God's household and service as permanent change of masters
boundary_disagreement: Book makes Jubilee structure plus permanent new mastery definitional and exclusive; consensus treats Jubilee as common type/alternative and primary as broader NT spiritual freedom (while still rejecting license).
rationale: Cores share the same central referent (release from bondage into God's service, rejecting license). Book preserves that category but materially narrows precision and extension by elevating the Jubilee image to definitional status and requiring 'change of masters, never the absence of one' as essential constitution; this reclassifies/excludes freer or non-Jubilee framings admitted in the broader consensus primary and its alternatives without replacing the referent.
strongest_objection: Consensus centers a more general NT spiritual-freedom description (with Jubilee as type or common alt) rather than making Jubilee the definitional core, so the book's framing may over-specify or re-center the primary identification.
